label: NY SHIELD § 899-bb — Reasonable security
body: 2.(a) Any person or business that owns or licenses computerized data which includes private information of a resident of New York shall develop, implement and maintain reasonable safeguards to protect the security, confidentiality and integrity of the private information including, but not limited to, disposal of data.
2.(b)(ii) A program is reasonable if it includes:

(A) Administrative safeguards — designate employee(s) to coordinate; identify foreseeable risks; assess sufficiency of safeguards; train employees; select service providers capable of maintaining appropriate safeguards (require by contract); adjust the program for business changes.
(B) Technical safeguards — assess risks in network/software design, in info processing/transmission/storage; detect/prevent/respond to attacks; regularly test and monitor controls.
(C) Physical safeguards — assess risks of storage/disposal; detect/prevent intrusions; protect against unauthorized access; dispose of private information so it cannot be read or reconstructed.
2.(c) A small business (fewer than 50 employees; <$3M revenue last three years; or <$5M assets) complies if its program contains safeguards appropriate for size, complexity, scope, and sensitivity.
